title: Lessons Learnt and New Processes following Review into Megan Khung Case
what_it_is: Lessons Learnt and New Processes following Review into Megan Khung Case

sections.label: Child abuse review panel measures
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry considers the review panel's proposed measures sufficient or will implement stronger reforms, and asks the CPS removal threshold and how the framework handles pushback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development given the review panel’s findings of the February 2020 fatal child abuse case, whether the Ministry considers the proposed measures sufficient or will stronger reforms such as independent oversight, real-time case-tracking, and statutory reporting duties be implemented to close systemic gaps especially in cases of suspected child abuse and domestic violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the threshold that the Child Protective Service (CPS) use to remove a child from the family; and (b) how does the framework deal with pushback and questions on why CPS is seen to intervene too early.

sections.label: Mandatory child safety reporting framework
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will consider a mandatory child safety reporting framework imposing a legal duty on designated persons aware of a child at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will consider introducing a mandatory child safety reporting framework to impose a legal duty on designated relevant persons who become aware of a child at risk to report such cases to the authorities.

sections.label: Review panel timing and future deaths
sections.summary: Asks why no review panel was convened before the 8 April 2025 statement and whether panels will be convened and published for future child protection deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) why the Ministry did not convene a review panel on the February 2020 fatal child abuse case in the intervening years before its statement on 8 April 2025 despite early indications that Child Protective Service was consulted; and (b) whether the Ministry will convene a review panel and publish its findings for any death in the child protection ecosystem in future.

sections.label: Digital system, community vigilance, removal criteria
sections.summary: Asks about a centralised risk flagging digital system, community programmes for neighbours, volunteers and grandparents, and criteria guiding child removal from family care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in view of the recent review of the child protection ecosystem, whether the Ministry will outline a plan for implementing a centralised, risk flagging digital system for at-risk children to provide authorised professional with a holistic view of a child's situation and ensuring that no crucial detail is missed between agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in light of the February 2020 fatal child abuse case, whether the Ministry will develop and facilitate community programmes for neighbours, volunteers, and grandparents to encourage community-based vigilance in recognising early signs of distress in families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what criteria guide the Ministry officers in determining when a child should be removed from family care due to suspected abuse; and (b) whether the Ministry will review these criteria, risk matrix, and workflows to ensure timely intervention.

sections.label: Inter-agency coordination in child protection
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry plans to strengthen inter-agency coordination, communication and risk assessment criteria among CPS, SPF, Social Services Agencies and Schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development given the Review Panel's findings and recommendations of the February 2020 fatal child abuse incident, whether the Ministry plans to strengthen and align inter-agency coordination, communication and risk assessment criteria between the agencies in the child protection ecosystem, such as Child Protection Services (CPS), SPF, Social Services Agencies and Schools in their management of child abuse reports and cases.

sections.label: Agencies accept panel findings on Megan
sections.summary: Agencies accept the Panel's findings in full, apologise for the outcome and lapses at CPS and SPF, and missed opportunities at ECDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All the agencies concerned – the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) Child Protective Service, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA), the Singapore Police Force (SPF), Beyond Social Services and HEART@Fei Yue Child Protection Specialist Centre – accept the Panel’s findings in full.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There were opportunities to pick up on the abuse, which might have prevented Megan’s death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On behalf of all the agencies and organisations concerned, we are deeply sorry for the outcome and for the lapses at the Child Protective Service and SPF, as well as the missed opportunities at ECDA.

sections.label: Megan's death prompted protocol enhancements
sections.summary: Megan's death five years ago had already prompted further enhancements to protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Megan’s death five years ago had already prompted further enhancements to protocols.

sections.label: Caseload ratios and child protection officers
sections.summary: Caseload ratios stayed around 18 to 21 cases per worker, while child protection officers doubled from around 45 in 2019 to more than 90 in 2040, bringing average caseload down from around 40 to 35.

sentences.text: Over the past three years, the average caseload ratio for the sector has been fairly stable at around 18 to 21 cases per worker, but the variation across centres is significant, ranging from 12 to 30 cases per worker.

For the Child Protective Service, now known as PSV or Protective Service, we have doubled our child protection officers from around 45 in 2019 to more than 90 in 2040, and we are continuing to expand.

[Please refer to ​clarification made under "Measures for Prompt Police Case Resolution and Mandating Assignment of Police Officers with Child Protection Training in Child-related Cases", Official Report, 5 November 2025, Vol 96, Issue 10, Oral Answers to Questions section.] The additional resources have helped bring down the average caseload per officer, down from around 40 to 35 today.

sections.label: New social service coordination centre
sections.summary: MSF will set up a new social service coordination centre supported by technology.

sentences.text: Indeed, MSF will be setting up a new social service coordination centre supported by technology.

sections.label: Three areas and implementation timeline
sections.summary: The three broad areas are improving role clarity, fostering a learning culture and providing structured support, with implementation to be completed by end 2026.

sentences.text: They focus on three broad areas: first, improving the clarity of roles within the child protection ecosystem; second, fostering a stronger learning culture; and third, providing more structured support for social service practitioners.
We will consult and work closely with the social sector to implement the recommendations progressively and complete the implementation by end 2026.

sections.label: Triage Assessment Panel appeals mechanism
sections.summary: MSF will set up a Triage Assessment Panel by the first quarter of 2026 to address cases where agencies differ on risk levels and case management.

sentences.text: In Recommendation 2, the Panel proposed establishing an appeals mechanism to address cases where agencies have differing views on risk levels and case management.
So, MSF will set up a Triage Assessment Panel by the first quarter of 2026 to do this and to determine which agency is best placed to manage the case, and then move.
